findings.evidence: Reviewer matrix: the PR's tools (docs/backlog/runtime-js/reference/pr-421-browser-fatal-matrix/) plus 13 reviewer kinds × file/-e (dependency throw, getter prop, listener log-and-rethrow, handled listener, rejection listener, throwing stack getter, cause chain, async fn, exitCode then throw, AggregateError, undefined, symbol, function) = 135 cells per host, run in /tmp/rev421 @ 25ef4d63c and in a fresh worktree of main 11b9397ee (pnpm install --offline); outputs /tmp/nf-review/matrix/{head,main}-{nocoi,coi}.json; node /tmp/nf-review/scripts/compare.mjs nocoi|coi → "cells 135 equal main 126 differ 9" on both hosts; node /tmp/nf-review/scripts/linediff.mjs → each of the 9 differs only in one rifty runtime frame line (8×: main's "at Object.import (<runtime>/packages/runtime-js/src/module-loader/loader.ts:L:C)" absent; file:sync:compile: "at importNodeMain (<runtime>/…/node-entry-main.ts)" instead of main's "at Object.import … / at runNodeEntry …").
findings.summary: The 7 (with reviewer cells 9) differing cells: only a rifty-internal frame line — main's `at Object.import (loader.ts)` is absent because the main-module claim enters the loader below `loader.import`. Under the criterion's letter this is outside the tolerance (only wrapper-induced USER frame changes); I judge it acceptable (rifty-internal frames are not guest-observable contract; main prints them only as an implementation leak), but the criterion record (ADR-0445 round-5 line / the proof doc) should say internal frame lines may differ — or route importNodeMain through loader.import to make the cells equal.

findings.evidence: Reviewer matrix: the PR's tools (docs/backlog/runtime-js/reference/pr-421-browser-fatal-matrix/) plus 13 reviewer kinds × file/-e (dependency throw, getter prop, listener log-and-rethrow, handled listener, rejection listener, throwing stack getter, cause chain, async fn, exitCode then throw, AggregateError, undefined, symbol, function) = 135 cells per host, run in /tmp/rev421 @ 25ef4d63c and in a fresh worktree of main 11b9397ee (pnpm install --offline); outputs /tmp/nf-review/matrix/{head,main}-{nocoi,coi}.json; node /tmp/nf-review/scripts/compare.mjs nocoi|coi → "cells 135 equal main 126 differ 9" on both hosts; node /tmp/nf-review/scripts/linediff.mjs → each of the 9 differs only in one rifty runtime frame line (8×: main's "at Object.import (<runtime>/packages/runtime-js/src/module-loader/loader.ts:L:C)" absent; file:sync:compile: "at importNodeMain (<runtime>/…/node-entry-main.ts)" instead of main's "at Object.import … / at runNodeEntry …"). Without user-frame normalization (node /tmp/nf-review/scripts/userframes.mjs nocoi): wrapper-induced only — "at Object.eval (/m/rN/main.js:3:7)" → "at Object.<anonymous> (/m/rN/main.js:1:133)", dep frames 4:9 → 2:9; NOT wrapper-induced — listener log-and-rethrow from a timer: file "at eval (/m/rN/main.js:3:104)" → "at Timeout.eval [as _onTimeout] (/m/rN/main.js:1:230)", and -e "at eval ([eval]:1:104)" → "at Timeout.eval [as _onTimeout] ([eval]:1:104)" (Node: "at Timeout._onTimeout ([eval]:1:104)").
findings.summary: The matrix normalizes every user-frame name (incl. `[eval]`), broader than "changed by the module wrapper": it hides that on the browser hosts an error created in a timer callback prints `Timeout.eval [as _onTimeout]` — neither main's `eval` nor Node's `Timeout._onTimeout` — wherever its `stack` is printed (listener rethrow, a rejection created in a timer, console.error). Kept on purpose (proof doc: timer callbacks as Timeout#_onTimeout on every host) but not in compat/ADR; declare it and tighten the normalization to wrapper effects.
